hypothesis: If Darwin is right, Palaeozoic and Mesozoic fossil collections are found on continental crust and shelves and are essentially absent from true oceanic islands remote from continents, so present ocean basins were not previously continental land.
pass_criterion: Using PBDB collections dated Cambrian to Cretaceous (max_ma greater than 66), after excluding continental fragments, accreted terranes and reworked or ex-situ material: at most 2 distinct genuine oceanic-island localities (volcanic or atoll islands on oceanic crust far from continental shelves, e.g. Hawaii, Azores, Galapagos, Ascension, St Helena, Tristan da Cunha) yield in-place Palaeozoic or Mesozoic collections, and these make up under 5% of the Silurian-to-Cretaceous collections located off continental shelves.
fail_criterion: More than 5 distinct genuine oceanic-island localities (same exclusions) yield in-place Palaeozoic or Mesozoic collections, or such islands account for 5% or more of the Silurian-to-Cretaceous collections located off continental shelves. A count of 3 to 5 localities is inconclusive.
interpretation: Darwin's 'oceanic island' means volcanic or coral islands on oceanic crust far from continents, not continental fragments such as Madagascar, New Zealand, the Seychelles or New Caledonia. 'Palaeozoic or Secondary formations' maps to PBDB collections with ages from Cambrian to Cretaceous. Only the premise-and-inference Darwin states is tested, which is the absence of old strata on oceanic islands implying long-standing ocean basins. Modern plate tectonics shows that the present ocean floor is younger than about 180 Ma, and that accreted oceanic terranes and ophiolites carry Palaeozoic and Mesozoic material. So the data may show exceptions, which will be reported separately and not counted as genuine oceanic-island localities. A pass confirms only the absence-of-old-strata premise. It does not confirm permanence of the whole ocean and continent configuration, which plate tectonics refutes.

dataset.name: The Paleobiology Database
dataset.why_it_fits: PBDB has a public data service API and download generator for fossil collections. Fields to use are lng, lat, early_interval, late_interval, max_ma, min_ma, cc (country code), geoplate, paleolng and paleolat, and formation, to locate Palaeozoic and Mesozoic collections on oceanic islands.
